findings.title: Google Meet fallback throws when no destination calendar is set
findings.body: The Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback used to read destinationCalendar?.integration, so a missing calendar evaluated to undefined and was replaced with Cal Video. It now destructures the first element of the new array and reads .integration with no null check. handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and confirm.handler sets []. Both become an empty array here, so mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the fallback can run. Any Google Meet booking that has no destination calendar — the case this branch exists for — now fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are discarded when the main calendar is null
findings.body: Co-host destination calendars are collected into teamDestinationCalendars, then appended with evt.destinationCalendar?.push. The field is set to null when the event type and the organizer both lack a destination calendar, and optional push on null does nothing, so every co-host calendar just collected is dropped. createAllCalendarEvents then sees no destinations. Its empty-list fallback only keeps credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches real types such as google_calendar, so nobody gets a calendar event. Even when the array is non-null, a host is included only if user.destinationCalendar is already set and schedulingType is COLLECTIVE, so a connected calendar with no destination-calendar row, and dynamic multi-user bookings without that scheduling type, still never get events. Initialize an array before pushing, and do not rely on the null optional chain.

findings.title: Each host create still targets only the first destination calendar
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination, but always passes the original event whose destinationCalendar array still lists every host. Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts around line 129), Office 365 (office365calendar CalendarService.ts around line 75), and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 162) only read index 0. Later iterations therefore use the co-host's token against the first host's calendar id. Office 365 and Lark fail that write; CalDAV filters to the foreign URL, matches nothing, and still returns a successful uid, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. The no-credentialId branch at line 380 also calls createEvent without destination.externalId and for every credential of that integration type, which duplicates events and cannot reach other hosts' credentials. If a credential cannot be loaded or has no app.slug, that host is skipped with no error result, so the booking still succeeds. updateAllCalendarEvents (line 542) passes the same unsplit event into every update, so reschedule has the same index-0 problem whenever a service falls back to destinationCalendar[0]. This is the stated acceptance criterion (every host calendar app should receive the event) and it does not hold for non-Google calendars.

findings.title: Google organizer email is always the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent now picks the calendar to write by matching credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still taken from destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId). The same event object, containing every host, is passed on every call, so an event written onto a co-host's calendar lists the primary host's calendar externalId as organizer. updateEvent (line 228) does the same on reschedule and location updates. Google can reject a write whose organizer does not match the authenticated calendar, or save an event with the wrong organizer and guest list, so co-host Google events are wrong even when calendarId selection succeeds. Select the destination entry that matches the credential or externalCalendarId being written, or pass a one-element destinationCalendar for that host.

findings.title: Cancelling a recurring series does not delete co-host calendar events
findings.body: When all remaining instances of a recurring booking are cancelled, the new per-reference loop still uses the old recurring body. That body ignores the reference and credential just resolved (including a co-host credential loaded from the database) and instead walks only the booking owner's calendar credentials. For each instance it uses references.find, so only the first calendar reference is deleted, and that delete is repeated once per owner credential and once per outer reference. Co-host credentials are never used, so their events stay on their calendars and keep blocking availability after the series is cancelled. Delete every calendar reference of every updated instance with that reference's own credentialId, and do not nest that work inside the outer reference loop.

findings.title: Organization slug is now set in the opposite billing case
findings.body: This unrelated edit inverts when an organization slug is stored. Previously slug was written on the team when team billing was disabled, and only metadata.requestedSlug was stored when billing was enabled so the slug could be assigned after payment. The new condition sets slug only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, and sets nothing when it is false. The requestedSlug line was not inverted, so billing-enabled creates now set both slug and requestedSlug. Self-hosted orgs (billing flag off) are created with no slug and cannot be resolved by subdomain. Billing-enabled orgs claim the slug immediately while still unverified, which conflicts with the deferred-slug flow. Restore slug when billing is disabled, and only requestedSlug when it is enabled.

findings.title: New booking references drop video credentialId and some external calendar ids
findings.body: referencesToCreate used to store evt.destinationCalendar.externalId for calendar results and result.credentialId for non-calendar results. It now stores result.externalId and, for anything that is not a calendar type, hardcodes credentialId to undefined. createAllCalendarEvents only passes destination.externalId into createEvent when destination.credentialId is set (line 370). The legacy branch at line 380 calls createEvent(c, event) with no external id, so those references are saved with externalCalendarId undefined. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference's credentialId is set, so if the video EventResult carried credentialId — which this mapping used to persist — cancelling a booking no longer deletes the remote meeting. Calendar references missing externalCalendarId also cannot be updated or deleted on the right calendar, especially with the broken Google fallback.

findings.title: Location change saves calendar references without calendar ids
findings.body: updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from result.externalId and result.credentialId. Calendar updates come from updateEvent, whose EventResult does not set externalId, credentialId, or createdEvent (CalendarManager.updateEvent only returns updatedEvent). Previously this mapping copied evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId onto every new reference. editLocation.handler persists referencesToCreate with references.create, so each location edit now inserts calendar rows with an empty uid and no externalCalendarId or credentialId. Later cancel/update cannot target the calendar those rows refer to, and deleteEvent may be called with an empty uid. Copy the reference's existing externalCalendarId and credentialId (or return them from updateEvent) instead of reading fields update results do not populate.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to a missing id
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent used to fall back to destinationCalendar.externalId. It now does destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). That find only runs when externalCalendarId is already null or empty, so it looks for a calendar whose externalId is null and never matches. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (line 317) has the same find, then falls back to "primary", so a cancellation of an event that lives on a non-primary calendar and whose booking reference has no externalCalendarId hits primary, gets a 404, and is swallowed — the event stays on the user's calendar and continues to block time. Fall back to the destination entry for this credential, or to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, not to a comparison against the missing id.

findings.title: A missing calendar credential fails every calendar update
findings.body: The new update loop loads a credential by reference.credentialId, but if it is still missing (deleted credential, or app.slug absent so the DB object is ignored) it still calls updateEvent(credential, ...) with credential undefined. createAllCalendarEvents guards with if (credential); this path does not. updateEvent then rejects, Promise.all rejects, and the catch treats every calendar reference as failed even if other updates already ran. The catch builds an error message and no longer logs it (console.error was removed), so the failure is silent in logs. Skip or record a per-reference failure when the credential cannot be loaded, and do not abort the rest of the batch.

findings.title: Merging a reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: When newBookingId is set, updateAllCalendarEvents now updates every calendar reference, but the following cleanup still uses booking.references.find for a single _calendar reference and deletes only that one, and only if it has a credentialId. Co-host events created by this PR are left on their calendars after a seated merge/reschedule, so those slots stay busy. If the first reference has no credentialId, none of the old events are deleted. Delete every old calendar reference, using each reference's credentialId.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking still schedules one calendar
findings.body: confirmHandler builds the CalendarEvent passed to handleConfirmation with only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar, wrapped in a one-element array. Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation (handleNewBooking connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]), and this handler never loads the other hosts' destination calendars. handleConfirmation is not updated in this PR to expand hosts itself, so a collective event that requires confirmation still creates a calendar event only for that one calendar. Co-hosts do not get events on confirm, which is the bug this change is supposed to fix for any booking that is not immediately accepted.

findings.title: PayPal confirmation creates events for only one calendar
findings.body: On payment success this builds evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's user.destinationCalendar only, then, when the booking is already accepted, calls eventManager.create(evt). That is a single calendar. The in-memory multi-host list from handleNewBooking is not stored on the booking (only the first destination calendar is connected), and this webhook does not load event-type hosts. Paid collective bookings whose calendar events are created here still invite only one host.

findings.title: Stripe confirmation creates events for only one calendar
findings.body: handlePaymentSuccess sets destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner only, then calls eventManager.create(evt) when the booking is already accepted. getBooking (line 119) does the same, and handleSetupSuccess uses that evt to create events when confirmation is not required. Neither path loads other collective hosts' destination calendars, and the booking row only has the first destination calendar connected. Paid or setup-intent collective bookings therefore still create a calendar event for one host only.

findings.title: Reschedule request deletes co-host events with the acting user's token
findings.body: Requesting a reschedule cancels the booking and deletes calendar events, but credentials are keyed only by credential.type from the acting user (credentialsMap.set(credential.type, credential)), not by reference.credentialId. A co-host reference whose type the actor also has (for example google_calendar) is deleted with the actor's token and the co-host's event uid. Google treats the resulting 404 as success, so the co-host event is left in place and the slot stays busy. References whose type the actor does not have are skipped entirely, with no database credential lookup. handleCancelBooking was updated to delete each reference with its own credential; this path was not, so collective events created by this PR are not removed from co-host calendars when a reschedule is requested.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar changed from object to array
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, and webhook payloads spread that evt (the playwright BOOKING_* assertions include this field). Existing consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will get undefined, because those fields are on the object, not the array. The PR describes this as a non-breaking bugfix, but it is a public payload break with no versioning. Producers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when unset, while confirm and the payment webhooks send []. BOOKING_REJECTED in webhook.e2e.ts now expects [] and BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so clients cannot null-check the field reliably.

findings.title: No test covers multi-host calendar create, update, or delete
findings.body: The only test change rewrites the BOOKING_REJECTED webhook fixture from destinationCalendar null to []. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes an event to each host's calendar, stores a reference with that host's credentialId and externalCalendarId, updates those events on reschedule, and deletes all of them on cancel — including non-Google calendars, a missing organizer destination calendar, recurring cancel-all, and payment or confirmation flows. The PR checklist notes that no such test was added. The bugs in this change (null push dropping co-host calendars, services always using index 0, recurring cancel deleting only the first reference) would not be caught in CI.
